newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly up, off new record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly up, off new record.

text.p: Swiss shares ended slightly firmer in slack trade on Monday after profit taking erased most early gains.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) slipped below the technically and psychologically important level of 3,900 points after posting an intra-day record high of 3,906.2 points.

Volumes were described as low. "It was a typical Monday bourse", a dealer said. Investors were cautious given the record levels on Wall Street. "But even if there is a correction in New York, it will probably not mar good sentiment here", he aded.
The SMI ended higher at 8.8 points, or 0.23 percent, at 3,891.6. All-share SPI firmed 3.69 points to 2,485.28.
Investors concentrated on major pharmaceuticals Roche, Ciba and Sandoz. Ciba and Sandoz added 0.5 percent and 0.74 percent to 1,600 francs and 1,507 francs, respectively.

Rumours the two firms would soon get expected approval from U.S. authorities to merge to form Novartis upheld the stocks, one dealer noted. Dealers warned of possible profit-taking if and when the approval is granted.
Roche certificates fell 10 francs to 10,010 francs.
UBS added five francs to 1,270 as markets continued speculating the bank would announce significant restructuring in Switzerland at a news conference on Tuesday.
One dealer said he did not believe UBS would announce sweeping changes on Tuesday. SBC jumped more than one percent to 259.25.

Among major industrials, Alusuisse and Holderbank firmed around 0.3 percent each. ABB ended unchanged at 1,630. Sulzer slid five francs to 755. Sulzer said it would offer registered shares in electronics unit Elma at 275 Swiss francs each when it spins off the company from December 4.
Swissair climbed more than two percent to 990.

On the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), options on UBS saw active trade. This was due to Tuesday's autumn news conference, one dealer noted. Around 14,000 UBS calls and 4,000 UBS puts were traded. Interest was also high in Ciba and Sandoz options.
Overall trade was quiet with 116,698 options traded. The call put ratio was 1.64 to one. Implicit volatilities were slightly higher.
In all, 28,489 SMI options and 3,481 SMI futures were traded. December Conf futures ended down ten basis points at 114.95.
